blocks.text: 16. HOW SUPPLIED/STORAGE AND HANDLING
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STEQEYMA (ustekinumab-stba) injection is a sterile, preservative-free, clear to very slightly opalescent, and colorless to pale yellow solution. It is supplied as individually packaged, singledose prefilled syringes or single-dose vials.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: For Subcutaneous Use
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Prefilled Syringes
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Each prefilled syringe is equipped with a 27-gauge fixed ½ inch thin wall needle, a needle safety guard, and a needle cover that is not made with natural rubber latex.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Single-dose Vial
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: For Intravenous Infusion
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Single-dose Vial
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Storage and Stability
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials and prefilled syringes refrigerated between 2ºC to 8ºC (36ºF to 46ºF). Store STEQEYMA vials upright. Keep the product in the original carton to protect from light until the time of use. Do not freeze. Do not shake.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If needed, individual vials and prefilled syringes may be stored at room temperature up to 30°C (86°F) for a maximum single period of up to 15 days in the original carton to protect from light. Record the date when the vial or the prefilled syringe is first removed from the refrigerator on the carton in the space provided. Once a vial or a syringe has been stored at room temperature, do not return to the refrigerator. Discard the vial or syringe if not used within 15 days at room temperature storage. Do not use STEQEYMA after the expiration date on the carton or on the vial or the prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 17. PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Advise the patient and/or caregiver to read the FDA-approved patient labeling (Medication Guide and Instructions for Use).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Inform patients that STEQEYMA may lower the ability of their immune system to fight infections and to contact their healthcare provider immediately if they develop any signs or symptoms of infection [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Malignancies
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Inform patients of the risk of developing malignancies while receiving STEQEYMA [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Serious Hypersensitivity and Reactions
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Inform patients that serious hypersensitivity reactions have been reported with intravenous and subcutaneous administration of ustekinumab products. Instruct patients to discontinue STEQEYMA and seek immediate medical attention if they experience any signs or symptoms of hypersensitivity reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Inform patients to immediately contact their healthcare provider if they experience signs and symptoms of PRES (which may include headache, seizures, confusion, or visual disturbances) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Immunizations

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STEQEYMA is a medicine that affects your immune system. STEQEYMA can increase your risk of having serious side effects, including:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Serious infections. STEQEYMA may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Some people have serious infections during treatment with ustekinumab products, including tuberculosis (TB), and infections caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses. Some people have to be hospitalized for treatment of their infection.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Your healthcare provider should check you for TB before starting STEQEYMA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If your healthcare provider feels that you are at risk for TB, you may be treated with medicine for TB before you begin treatment with STEQEYMA and during treatment with STEQEYMA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB while you are being treated with STEQEYMA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You should not start STEQEYMA if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider says it is okay.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: After starting STEQEYMA, call your healthcare provider right away if you have any symptoms of an infection (see above). These may be signs of infections such as chest infections, or skin infections or shingles that could have serious complications. STEQEYMA can make you more likely to get infections or make an infection that you have worse.
section_path: Before starting STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider if you:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: People who have a genetic problem where the body does not make any of the proteins interleukin 12 (IL-12) and interleukin 23 (IL-23) are at a higher risk for certain serious infections. These infections can spread throughout the body and cause death. People who take STEQEYMA may also be more likely to get these infections.
section_path: Before starting STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider if you:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Cancers. STEQEYMA may decrease the activity of your immune system and increase your risk for certain types of cancers. Tell your healthcare provider if you have ever had any type of cancer. Some people who are receiving ustekinumab products and have risk factors for skin cancer have developed certain types of skin cancers. During your treatment with STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider if you develop any new skin growths.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What is STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STEQEYMA is a prescription medicine used to treat:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: adults and children 6 years of age and older with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or phototherapy (treatment using ultraviolet light alone or with pills).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: adults and children 6 years of age and older with active psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known if STEQEYMA is safe and effective in children with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis or in children less than 6 years of age with plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Who should not use STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA if you are allergic to ustekinumab products or any of the ingredients in STEQEYMA. See the end of this Medication Guide for a complete list of ingredients in STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item

section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). People who are being treated with STEQEYMA should avoid receiving live vaccines. Tell your healthcare provider if anyone in your house needs a live vaccine. The viruses used in some types of live vaccines can spread to people with a weakened immune system, and can cause serious problems. You should avoid receiving the BCG vaccine during the one year before receiving STEQEYMA or one year after you stop receiving STEQEYMA.
section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: have any new or changing lesions within psoriasis areas or on normal skin.
section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: are receiving or have received allergy shots, especially for serious allergic reactions. Allergy shots may not work as well for you during treatment with STEQEYMA. STEQEYMA may also increase your risk of having an allergic reaction to an allergy shot.
section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

blocks.text: are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if STEQEYMA can harm your unborn baby. You and your healthcare provider should decide if you will receive STEQEYMA.
section_path: Before you use or receive STEQEYMA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: How should I use STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use STEQEYMA exactly as the healthcare provider tells you to. The healthcare provider will determine the right dose of STEQEYMA, the amount for each injection, and how often it should be given. Be sure to keep all scheduled follow-up appointments.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Adults with Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis will receive the first dose of STEQEYMA through a vein in the arm (intravenous infusion) in a healthcare facility by a healthcare provider. It takes at least 1 hour to receive the full dose of medicine. STEQEYMA will then be received as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) 8 weeks after the first dose of STEQEYMA, as described below.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Adults and children 6 years of age and older with plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis will receive STEQEYMA as an injection under the skin as described below.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Injecting STEQEYMA under the skin
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o STEQEYMA is intended for use under the guidance and supervision of a healthcare provider.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o In children, it is recommended that STEQEYMA be administered by a healthcare provider. If a healthcare provider decides that you or a caregiver may give the injections of STEQEYMA at home, you or a caregiver should receive training on the right way to prepare and inject STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Do not try to inject STEQEYMA until you have been shown how to inject STEQEYMA by a healthcare provider.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o STEQEYMA can be injected under the skin in the upper arms, buttocks, upper legs (thighs) or stomach area (abdomen).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Use a different injection site each time you use STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If you inject too much STEQEYMA, call the healthcare provider or Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222, or go to the nearest emergency room right away.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Read the detailed Instructions for Use at the end of this Medication Guide for instructions about how to prepare and inject a dose of STEQEYMA, and how to properly throw away (dispose of) used needles, syringes, and vials. The syringe, needle, and vial must never be re-used. After the rubber stopper is punctured, STEQEYMA can become contaminated by harmful bacteria which could cause an infection if reused. Therefore, throw away any unused portion of STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: How should I store STEQEYMA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials and prefilled syringes in a refrigerator between 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials standing up straight (upright).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA in the original carton to protect it from light until time to use it.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not freeze STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If needed, individual STEQEYMA vials and prefilled syringes may also be stored at room temperature up to 86ºF (30°C) for a maximum single period of up to 15 days in the original carton to protect from light.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Record the date when the vial or the prefilled syringe is first removed from the refrigerator on the carton in the space provided.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After a vial or a syringe has been stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw away (discard) the vial or syringe if not used within 15 days at room temperature storage.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA after the expiration date on the carton or on the vial or the prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Keep STEQEYMA and all medicines out of the reach of children.

You can ask your pharmacist or healthcare provider for information about STEQEYMA that was written for health professionals.

blocks.text: The STEQEYMA vial is for single-use only (see Figure A). It contains 45 mg of STEQEYMA for injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Figure A
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Before you start, check the carton to make sure that it is the right dose. You will have either 45 mg or 90 mg as prescribed by the healthcare provider.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is 45 mg or less you will receive one 45 mg vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is 90 mg, you will receive two 45 mg vials, and you will need to give two injections, one right after the other.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the expiration date on the vial and carton. If the expiration date has passed, do not use it. If the expiration date has passed, call the healthcare provider or pharmacist, or call 1-888-804-3433 for help.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the vial for any particles or discoloration. The liquid in the vial should look clear to very slightly opalescent and colorless to pale yellow.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA if it is frozen, discolored, cloudy or has particles. Get a new vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake the vial at any time. Shaking the vial may damage the STEQEYMA medicine. If your vial has been shaken, do not use it. Get a new vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use a STEQEYMA vial more than one time, even if there is medicine left in the vial. After the rubber stopper is punctured, STEQEYMA can become contaminated by harmful bacteria which could cause an infection if re-used. Therefore, throw away any unused STEQEYMA after you give the injection.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Safely throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA vials, needles, and syringes after use. See "Step 20: Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA."
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not re-use syringes or needles.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: To avoid needle-stick injuries, do not recap needles.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Storing STEQEYMA vials
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials in a refrigerator between 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials standing up straight (upright).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA vials in the original carton to protect from light until the time of use.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not freeze STEQEYMA vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If needed, individual vials may be stored at room temperature up to 86°F (30°C) for a maximum single period of up to 15 days in the original carton to protect from light.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Record the date when the vial is first removed from the refrigerator on the carton in the space provided.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After a vial has been stored at room temperature, it should not be returned to the refrigerator.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw away (discard) the vial if not used within 15 days at room temperature storage.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA after the expiration date on the carton or on the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Keep STEQEYMA vial and all medicines out of the reach of children.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Leave the carton containing the STEQEYMA vial at room temperature 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C) for 30 minutes to allow it to warm up (see Figure D).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not warm the vial using heat sources such as hot water or a microwave.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item

blocks.text: Step 5. Inspect the STEQEYMA vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Look at the vial and make sure you have the correct medicine (STEQEYMA) and dosage.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Look at the vial and make sure it is not cracked or damaged.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA if the vial has been dropped or damaged.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the expiration date on the label of the vial (see Figure F).

blocks.text: Step 6. Inspect the medicine.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Look at the medicine in the vial to make sure that the liquid is clear to very slightly opalescent and colorless to pale yellow. (see Figure G).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA if the liquid is discolored or cloudy, or if it contains visible flakes or particles.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure H).
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure H).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Choose an injection site around the stomach area (abdomen), buttocks, and upper legs (thighs). If a caregiver is giving the injection, the outer area of the upper arms may also be used.
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure H).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use a different injection site for each injection.
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure H).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard. If possible, do not use areas of skin that show signs of psoriasis.

blocks.text: Step 8. Clean the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Clean the skin with an alcohol wipe where you plan to give the injection (see Figure I).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch this area again before giving the injection. Let the skin dry before injecting.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not fan or blow on the clean area.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: Step 9. Remove the protective cap from the vial.
section_path: Step 9. Remove the protective cap from the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Remove the protective cap from the STEQEYMA vial. Throw away the cap (see Figure J).
section_path: Step 9. Remove the protective cap from the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not remove the rubber stopper.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 10. Clean the rubber stopper.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Wipe the rubber stopper of the vial with an alcohol wipe and allow it to dry (see Figure K).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch the rubber stopper after you clean it.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Put the vial on a flat surface.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the syringe at the middle of the syringe body with the needle pointing away from yourself, and pull the needle cap straight off the syringe (see Figure L).
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw away (dispose of) the needle cap right away in an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container (see Step 20. Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA).
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not re-cap the syringe.
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not touch the needle or let the needle touch anything. Doing so may result in a needle stick injury.
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use the syringe if it has been dropped without the needle cap in place. Call your healthcare provider for further instructions.
section_path: Step 11. Remove the needle cap from the syringe.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 12. Draw air into the syringe.
section_path: Step 12. Draw air into the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Pull back on the plunger rod to draw air into the syringe equal to your STEQEYMA dose volume.
section_path: Step 12. Draw air into the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the vial between your thumb and index (pointer) finger.
section_path: Step 12. Draw air into the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Push the needle through the rubber stopper of the vial, and push the plunger rod to inject the air into the vial (see Figure M).
section_path: Step 12. Draw air into the syringe.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 13. Withdraw the correct dose.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Leave the needle in the vial and turn both the syringe and vial upside down (vial on top).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the syringe and vial firmly in one hand. Make sure the tip of the needle is in the STEQEYMA medicine.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: It is important that the needle tip is always in the medicine. This stops air bubbles from forming in the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: With your other hand, pull on the plunger rod to fill the syringe with the amount of medicine prescribed by the healthcare provider (see Figure N).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Fill the syringe until the black tip of the plunger lines up with the mark that matches your prescribed dose.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 14.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Check for air bubbles.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not remove the needle from the vial. Hold the syringe with the needle pointing up to see if it has any air bubbles inside.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If there are air bubbles, gently tap the side of the syringe until the air bubbles go to the top of the syringe (see Figure O).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Slowly press the plunger rod until all of the air bubbles (but none of the medicine) have been removed.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Remove the syringe from the vial. Do not lay the syringe down or allow the needle to touch anything.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: caption
blocks.text: Figure O

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Injecting STEQEYMA
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Hold the body of the syringe in one hand between the thumb and index fingers (see Figure P).
section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not pull back on the plunger rod at any time.
section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use the other hand to gently pinch the cleaned area of skin. Hold firmly. Note: Pinching the skin is important to make sure that you inject under the skin (into the fatty area) but not any deeper (into muscle).
section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use a quick and dart-like motion to insert the needle into the pinched skin at about a 45-degree angle (see Figure P).
section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer

section_path: Step 15. Insert the needle into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 16. Give the injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After the needle is inserted use your thumb to slowly and evenly push the plunger rod all the way to the bottom of the syringe body. Keep the skin gently pinched.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Make sure you have injected all of the STEQEYMA medicine (see Figure Q).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: caption
blocks.text: Figure Q
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 17. Remove the syringe from the injection site.
section_path: Step 17. Remove the syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After the syringe is empty, release the pinched skin and slowly pull the needle out of the injection site. (see Figure R).
section_path: Step 17. Remove the syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not re-cap the used needle. Recapping the used needle can lead to a needle-stick injury.
section_path: Step 17. Remove the syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not rub the injection site.
section_path: Step 17. Remove the syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: There may be some bleeding at the injection site. This is normal (see Step 18. Care for the injection site). ·

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: After the Injection
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
section_path: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not rub the injection site.
section_path: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: There may be a small amount of blood or liquid at the injection site. This is normal.
section_path: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If some bleeding occurs, you can press a cotton ball or gauze over the injection site and hold for 10 seconds.
section_path: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You may cover the injection site with a small adhesive bandage, if necessary.
section_path: Step 18. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 19. If your dose requires 2 injections, give the second injection right after the first.
section_path: Step 19. If your dose requires 2 injections, give the second injection right after the first.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If your dose is 90 mg, you will have two 45 mg vials. You will need to give a second injection right after the other.
section_path: Step 19. If your dose requires 2 injections, give the second injection right after the first.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Repeat Steps 5 to 18 for the second injection using a new vial and syringe with needle.
section_path: Step 19. If your dose requires 2 injections, give the second injection right after the first.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Choose a different site for the second injection.
section_path: Step 19. If your dose requires 2 injections, give the second injection right after the first.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 20. Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Put the used needle, syringe and vial in an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container right away after use (see Figure S).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not throw away (dispose of) the syringe in your household trash.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Never re-use needles and syringes, for your safety and health, and for the safety of others.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Alcohol wipes, and other supplies can be disposed of in your household trash.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If you do not have an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container, you may use a household container that is:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o made of a heavy-duty plastic,
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o can be closed with a tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid, without sharps being able to come out,
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o upright and stable during use,
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o leak-resistant, and
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o properly labeled to warn of hazardous waste inside the container.

blocks.label: list_item

blocks.text: Do not dispose of your used sharps disposal container in your household trash unless your community guidelines permit this. Do not recycle your used sharps disposal container.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: (ustekinumab-stba) injection, for subcutaneous use

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: This Instructions for Use contains information on how to inject STEQEYMA using a prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Read this Instructions for Use before you start using STEQEYMA. A healthcare provider should show you how to prepare and give an injection of STEQEYMA the right way.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: ask your healthcare provider to help you, or
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: ask someone who has been trained by a healthcare provider to give your injections.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not try to inject STEQEYMA until you have been shown how to inject STEQEYMA by a healthcare provider.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: For subcutaneous use only (inject directly under the skin).
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Before you start, check the carton to make sure that it is the right dose. You will have either 45 mg or 90 mg as prescribed by the healthcare provider.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is 45 mg, you will receive one 45 mg prefilled syringe.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is 90 mg, you will receive either one 90 mg prefilled syringe or two 45 mg prefilled syringes. If you receive two 45 mg prefilled syringes for a 90 mg dose, you will need to give two injections, one right after the other.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Check the expiration date on the prefilled syringe and carton. If the expiration date has passed or if the prefilled syringe has been kept at room temperature up to 86℉ (30℃) for longer than 15 days, do not use it. Call the healthcare provider or pharmacist, or call 1-888-804-3433 for help.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use the prefilled syringe if the liquid is discolored, cloudy, or has particles. Get a new prefilled syringe.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake the prefilled syringe at any time. Shaking the prefilled syringe may damage the STEQEYMA medicine. If the prefilled syringe has been shaken, do not use it. Get a new prefilled syringe.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: To reduce the risk of accidental needle sticks, each prefilled syringe has a needle safety guard that is automatically activated to cover the needle after you have given the injection. Do not pull back on the plunger rod at any time.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STEQEYMA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Storing STEQEYMA prefilled syringes
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA prefilled syringes in the refrigerator between 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8ºC).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Store STEQEYMA prefilled syringes in the original carton to protect from light.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not freeze STEQEYMA prefilled syringes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not shake STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: If needed, STEQEYMA prefilled syringe may be stored at room temperature up to 86℉ (30℃) for a maximum single period of up to 15 days in the original carton to protect from light.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Record the date when the prefilled syringe is removed from the refrigerator on the carton in the space provided.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After a prefilled syringe has been stored at room temperature, do not return it to the refrigerator.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Throw away (discard) the prefilled syringe if it is not used within 15 days at room temperature storage.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not use STEQEYMA after the expiration date on the carton or the prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Keep STEQEYMA and all medicines out of the reach of children.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text:  Prepare a clean, flat surface, such as a table or counter top, in a well-lit area.

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Take the carton(s) containing the prefilled syringe(s) needed to administer your prescribed dose out of the refrigerator. Each STEQEYMA carton contains 1 prefilled syringe.
section_path: Step 1. Gather the supplies for the injection
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Note: Depending on the dose prescribed to you by your healthcare provider you may need to prepare 1 or more prefilled syringes and inject the contents of them all.
section_path: Step 1. Gather the supplies for the injection

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 3. Wait 30 minutes.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Open the carton. Gripping from the syringe body, lift the prefilled syringe from the carton.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Leave the prefilled syringe outside of the carton at room temperature 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C) for 30 minutes to allow it to warm up (see Figure E).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not warm the prefilled syringe using heat sources such as hot water or a microwave.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the prefilled syringe does not reach room temperature, this could cause the injection to feel uncomfortable and make it hard to push the plunger.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 4. Wash your hands.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Wash your hands with soap and water and dry them thoroughly (see Figure F).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 5. Inspect the prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Look at the prefilled syringe and make sure you have the correct medicine (STEQEYMA) and dosage.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Look at the prefilled syringe and make sure it is not cracked or damaged.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Check the expiration date on the label of the prefilled syringe (see Figure G).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use if the expiration date has passed.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 6. Inspect the medicine.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Look at the medicine and make sure that the liquid is clear to very slightly opalescent and colorless to pale yellow. (see Figure H).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use the prefilled syringe if the liquid is discolored, cloudy, or has particles. Get a new prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  You may see air bubbles in the liquid. This is normal.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure I).
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure I).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Choose an injection site around the stomach area (abdomen), buttocks, upper legs (thighs). If a caregiver is giving the injection, the outer area of the upper arms may also be used (see Figure I).
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure I).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use a different injection site for each injection.
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure I).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.
section_path: Step 7. Choose an injection site (see Figure I).

blocks.text: Step 8. Clean the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Clean the skin with an alcohol wipe where you plan to give the injection (see Figure J).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not touch this area again before giving the injection. Let the skin dry before injecting.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not fan or blow on the clean area.

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If the dose is 90 mg, you will receive either one 90 mg prefilled syringe or two 45 mg prefilled syringes. If you receive two 45 mg prefilled syringes for a 90 mg dose, you will need to give a second injection right after the first.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 9. Remove the cap.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Remove the needle cap when you are ready to inject STEQEYMA by holding the body of the prefilled syringe in one hand between the thumb and index fingers (see Figure K).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not hold the plunger while removing the cap.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  You may see a few drops of liquid at the tip of the needle. This is normal.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Throw away (dispose of) the cap right away in an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container (see Step 13. Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not re-cap the prefilled syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not touch the needle. Doing so may result in a needle stick injury.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use the prefilled syringe if it has been dropped without the needle cover in place.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
section_path: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Hold the body of the prefilled syringe in one hand between the thumb and index fingers (see Figure L).
section_path: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not pull back on the plunger rod at any time.
section_path: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use the other hand to gently pinch the cleaned area of skin. Hold firmly. Note: Pinching the skin is important to make sure that you inject under the skin (into the fatty area) but not any deeper (into muscle).
section_path: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use a quick and dart-like motion to insert the needle into the pinched skin at about a 45-degree angle (see Figure L).
section_path: Step 10. Insert the prefilled syringe into the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 11. Give the injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After the needle is inserted, release the pinch.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Inject all of the liquid by using your thumb to push the plunger all the way down (see Figure M).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the plunger is not fully pressed, the needle safety guard will not extend to cover the needle when it is removed.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  After the prefilled syringe is empty, slowly lift your thumb from the plunger rod until the needle is completely covered by the needle safety guard (see Figure N).
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If the needle is not covered, proceed carefully to throw away (dispose of) the syringe (see Step 13. Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA).
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Some bleeding may occur. This is normal (see Step 14. Care for the injection site).
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not rub the injection site.
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Repeat Steps 1 to 12 for the second injection using a new syringe. Choose a different site for the second injection.
section_path: Step 12. Remove the prefilled syringe from the injection site.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 13. Throw away (dispose of) STEQEYMA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Put the used prefilled syringe in an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container right away after use (see Figure O).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  STEQEYMA prefilled syringe is a single-dose syringe and should not be used again.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not throw away (dispose of) the prefilled syringe in your household trash.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If you do not have an FDA-cleared sharps disposal container, you may use a household container that is:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o made of a heavy-duty plastic
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o can be closed with a tight-fitting, puncture-resistant lid, without sharps being able to come out.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o upright and stable during use,
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o leak-resistant,
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o and properly labeled to warn of hazardous waste inside the container.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  When your sharps disposal container is almost full, you will need to follow your community guidelines for the right way to dispose of it. There may be state or local laws about how you should throw away used needles and syringes. For more information about safe sharps disposal, and for specific information about sharps disposal in the state that you live in, go to the FDA's website at: http://www.fda.gov/safesharpsdisposal.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not dispose of your used sharps disposal container in your household trash unless your community guidelines permit this. Do not recycle your used sharps disposal container.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 14. Care for the injection site.
section_path: Step 14. Care for the injection site.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If some bleeding occurs, treat the injection site by gently pressing, not rubbing, a cotton ball or gauze to the site and apply an adhesive bandage if needed.
section_path: Step 14. Care for the injection site.

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Infections: Serious infections have occurred. Avoid starting Ustekinumab-stba during any clinically important active infection. If a serious infection or clinically significant infection develops, discontinue Ustekinumab-stba until the infection resolves. (5.1)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Theoretical Risk for Particular Infections: Serious infections from mycobacteria, salmonella, and Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinations have been reported in patients genetically deficient in IL12/IL-23. Consider diagnostic tests for these infections as dictated by clinical circumstances. (5.2)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Tuberculosis (TB): Evaluate patients for TB prior to initiating treatment with Ustekinumab-stba. Initiate treatment of latent TB before administering Ustekinumab-stba. (5.3)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Malignancies: Ustekinumab products may increase risk of malignancy. The safety of ustekinumab products in patients with a history of or a known malignancy has not been evaluated. (5.4)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions: If a severe or other clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue Ustekinumab-stba immediately and initiate appropriate medical treatment. (5.5)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES): If PRES is suspected, treat promptly, and discontinue Ustekinumab-stba. (5.6)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Immunizations: Avoid use of live vaccines in patients during treatment with Ustekinumab-stba. (5.7)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Noninfectious Pneumonia: Cases of interstitial pneumonia, eosinophilic pneumonia, and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia have been reported during post-approval use of ustekinumab products. If diagnosis is confirmed, discontinue Ustekinumab-stba and institute appropriate treatment. (5.8)

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 2.4. General Considerations for Administration
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Ustekinumab-stba is intended for use under the guidance and supervision of a healthcare provider. Ustekinumab-stba should only be administered to patients who will be closely monitored and have regular follow-up visits with a healthcare provider. The appropriate dose should be determined by a healthcare provider using the patient's current weight at the time of dosing. In pediatric patients, it is recommended that Ustekinumab-stba be administered by a healthcare provider. If a healthcare provider determines that it is appropriate, a patient may self-inject or a caregiver may inject Ustekinumab-stba after proper training in subcutaneous injection technique. Instruct patients to follow the directions provided in the Instructions for Use [see Instructions for Use].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: It is recommended that each injection be administered at a different anatomic location (such as upper arms, gluteal regions, thighs, or any quadrant of abdomen) than the previous injection, and not into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated. When using the vial, a 1 mL syringe with a 27 gauge, ½ inch needle is recommended.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Prior to administration, visually inspect Ustekinumab-stba for particulate matter and discoloration. Ustekinumab-stba is a clear to very slightly opalescent and colorless to pale yellow solution. Do not use Ustekinumab-stba if it is discolored or cloudy, or if other particulate matter is present. Ustekinumab-stba does not contain preservatives; therefore, discard any unused product remaining in the vial and/or syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: After withdrawing Ustekinumab-stba from the single-dose vial for subcutaneous use, administer the dose immediately. The vial does not contain preservatives. Discard any unused portion of drug remaining in the vial or syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: Infuse the diluted solution over a period of at least one hour. Once diluted, the infusion should be completely administered within four hours of the dilution in the infusion bag.
section_path: 2.5. Preparation and Administration of Ustekinumab-stba 130 mg/26 mL (5 mg/mL) Vial for Intravenous Infusion (Crohn's Disease and Ulcerative Colitis)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Use only an infusion set with an in-line, sterile, non-pyrogenic, low protein-binding filter (pore size 0.2 micrometer).

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Do not infuse Ustekinumab-stba concomitantly in the same intravenous line with other agents.

blocks.text: Ustekinumab-stba does not contain preservatives. Each vial is for a one-time use in only one patient. Discard any remaining solution. Dispose any unused medicinal product in accordance with local requirements.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 4. CONTRAINDICATIONS
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab-stba is contraindicated in patients with clinically significant hypersensitivity to ustekinumab products or to any of the excipients in Ustekinumab-stba [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5. WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.1. Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products may increase the risk of infections and reactivation of latent infections. Serious bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral infections were observed in patients receiving ustekinumab products [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serious infections requiring hospitalization, or otherwise clinically significant infections, reported in clinical trials included the following:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Plaque Psoriasis: diverticulitis, cellulitis, pneumonia, appendicitis, cholecystitis, sepsis, osteomyelitis, viral infections, gastroenteritis, and urinary tract infections.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Psoriatic arthritis: cholecystitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Crohn's disease: anal abscess, gastroenteritis, ophthalmic herpes zoster, pneumonia, and listeria meningitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Ulcerative colitis: gastroenteritis, ophthalmic herpes zoster, pneumonia, and listeriosis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Avoid initiating treatment with Ustekinumab-stba in patients with any clinically important active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated. Consider the risks and benefits of treatment prior to initiating use of Ustekinumab-stba in patients with a chronic infection or a history of recurrent infection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Instruct patients to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms suggestive of an infection occur while on treatment with Ustekinumab-stba and discontinue Ustekinumab-stba for serious or clinically significant infections until the infection resolves or is adequately treated.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.2. Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
section_path: 5.2. Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Individuals genetically deficient in IL-12/IL-23 are particularly vulnerable to disseminated infections from mycobacteria (including nontuberculous, environmental mycobacteria), salmonella (including nontyphi strains), and Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccinations. Serious infections and fatal outcomes have been reported in such patients.
section_path: 5.2. Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known whether patients with pharmacologic blockade of IL-12/IL-23 from treatment with ustekinumab products may be susceptible to these types of infections. Consider appropriate diagnostic testing (e.g., tissue culture, stool culture, as dictated by clinical circumstances).
section_path: 5.2. Theoretical Risk for Vulnerability to Particular Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.3. Pre-treatment Evaluation for Tuberculosis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Evaluate patients for tuberculosis infection prior to initiating treatment with Ustekinumab-stba.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Avoid administering Ustekinumab-stba to patients with active tuberculosis infection. Initiate treatment of latent tuberculosis prior to administering Ustekinumab-stba. Consider antituberculosis therapy prior to initiation of Ustekinumab-stba in patients with a past history of latent or active tuberculosis in whom an adequate course of treatment cannot be confirmed. Closely monitor patients receiving Ustekinumab-stba for signs and symptoms of active tuberculosis during and after treatment.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.4. Malignancies
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Ustekinumab products are immunosuppressants and may increase the risk of malignancy. Malignancies were reported among subjects who received ustekinumab in clinical trials [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)]. In rodent models, inhibition of IL-12/IL-23p40 increased the risk of malignancy [see Nonclinical Toxicology (13)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of ustekinumab products has not been evaluated in patients who have a history of malignancy or who have a known malignancy.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: There have been post-marketing reports of the rapid appearance of multiple cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas in patients receiving ustekinumab products who had pre-existing risk factors for developing non-melanoma skin cancer. Monitor all patients receiving Ustekinumab-stba for the appearance of non-melanoma skin cancer. Closely follow patients greater than 60 years of age, those with a medical history of prolonged immunosuppressant therapy and those with a history of PUVA treatment [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.5. Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and angioedema, have been reported with ustekinumab products in clinical trials and postmarketing. Some serious hypersensitivity reactions have occurred during the first intravenous dose of ustekinumab products [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If a severe or clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue Ustekinumab-stba immediately and initiate appropriate medical treatment [see Contraindications (4)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.6. Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Two cases of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), also known as Reversible Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome (RPLS), were reported in clinical trials. Cases have also been reported in postmarketing experience in patients with psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and Crohn's disease. Clinical presentation included headaches, seizures, confusion, visual disturbances, and imaging changes consistent with PRES a few days to several months after ustekinumab product initiation. A few cases reported latency of a year or longer. Patients recovered with supportive care following withdrawal of ustekinumab products.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Monitor all patients treated with Ustekinumab-stba for signs and symptoms of PRES. If PRES is suspected, promptly administer appropriate treatment and discontinue Ustekinumab-stba.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.7. Immunizations
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Prior to initiating therapy with Ustekinumab-stba, patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as recommended by current immunization guidelines. Patients being treated with Ustekinumab-stba should avoid receiving live vaccines. Avoid administering BCG vaccines during treatment with Ustekinumab-stba or for one year prior to initiating treatment or one year following discontinuation of treatment. Caution is advised when administering live vaccines to household contacts of patients receiving Ustekinumab-stba because of the potential risk for shedding from the household contact and transmission to patient.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Non-live vaccinations received during a course of Ustekinumab-stba may not elicit an immune response sufficient to prevent disease.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 5.8. Noninfectious Pneumonia
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Cases of interstitial pneumonia, eosinophilic pneumonia, and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia have been reported during post-approval use of ustekinumab products. Clinical presentations included cough, dyspnea, and interstitial infiltrates following one to three doses. Serious outcomes have included respiratory failure and prolonged hospitalization. Patients improved with discontinuation of therapy and in certain cases administration of corticosteroids. If diagnosis is confirmed, discontinue Ustekinumab-stba and institute appropriate treatment [see Postmarketing Experience (6.3)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6. ADVERSE REACTIONS
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The following serious adverse reactions are discussed elsewhere in the label:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Infections [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)]
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Malignancies [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4)]
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Serious Hypersensitivity Reactions [see Warnings and Precautions (5.5)]
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6)]
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: Noninfectious Pneumonia [see Warnings and Precautions (5.8)]
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: 6.1. Clinical Trials Experience
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Because clinical trials are conducted under widely varying conditions, adverse reaction rates observed in the clinical trials of a drug cannot be directly compared to rates in the clinical trials of another drug and may not reflect the rates observed in practice.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Adult Subjects with Plaque Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety data reflect exposure to ustekinumab in 3117 adult subjects with plaque psoriasis, including 2414 exposed for at least 6 months, 1855 exposed for at least one year, 1653 exposed for at least two years, 1569 exposed for at least three years, 1482 exposed for at least four years and 838 exposed for at least five years.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Table 5 summarizes the adverse reactions that occurred at a rate of at least 1% with higher rates in the ustekinumab groups during the placebo-controlled period of Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2 [see Clinical Studies (14)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.caption: Table 5: Adverse Reactions, Reported by ≥1% of Subjects with Plaque Psoriasis and at Higher Rates in the ustekinumab groups through Week 12 in Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: caption
blocks.text: Table 5: Adverse Reactions, Reported by ≥1% of Subjects with Plaque Psoriasis and at Higher Rates in the ustekinumab groups through Week 12 in Ps STUDY 1 and Ps STUDY 2
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Adverse reactions that occurred at rates less than 1% in the controlled period of Ps STUDIES 1 and 2 through week 12 included: cellulitis, herpes zoster, diverticulitis, and certain injection site reactions (pain, swelling, pruritus, induration, hemorrhage, bruising, and irritation).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: One case of PRES occurred during clinical trials in adult subjects with plaque psoriasis [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Infections
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the placebo-controlled period of clinical trials of subjects with plaque psoriasis (average followup of 12.6 weeks for subjects receiving placebo and 13.4 weeks for ustekinumab-treated subjects), 27% of ustekinumab-treated subjects reported infections (1.39 per patient-years of follow-up) compared with 24% of subjects receiving placebo (1.21 per patient-years of follow-up). Serious infections occurred in 0.3% of ustekinumab-treated subjects (0.01 per patient-years of follow-up) and in 0.4% of subjects receiving placebo (0.02 per patient-year of follow-up) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the controlled and non-controlled portions of clinical trials in subjects with plaque psoriasis (median follow-up of 3.2 years), representing 8998 patient-years of exposure, 72.3% of ustekinumab-treated subjects reported infections (0.87 per patient-years of follow-up). Serious infections were reported in 2.8% of subjects (0.01 per patient-years of follow-up).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Malignancies
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In the controlled and non-controlled portions of clinical trials in subjects with plaque psoriasis (median follow-up of 3.2 years, representing 8998 patient-years of exposure), 1.7% of ustekinumab-treated subjects reported malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancers (0.60 per hundred patient-years of follow-up). Non-melanoma skin cancer was reported in 1.5% of ustekinumab-treated subjects (0.52 per hundred patient-years of follow-up) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.4)]. The most frequently observed malignancies other than non-melanoma skin cancer during the clinical trials were: prostate, melanoma, colorectal and breast. Malignancies other than non-melanoma skin cancer in ustekinumab-treated subjects during the controlled and uncontrolled portions of trials were similar in type and number to what would be expected in the general U.S. population according to the SEER database (adjusted for age, gender and race). 1
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Pediatric Subjects with Plaque Psoriasis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of ustekinumab was assessed in two trials of pediatric subjects with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. Ps STUDY 3 evaluated safety for up to 60 weeks in 110 pediatric subjects 12 to 17 years old. Ps STUDY 4 evaluated safety for up to 56 weeks in 44 pediatric subjects 6 to 11 years old. The safety profile in pediatric subjects was similar to the safety profile from trials in adults with plaque psoriasis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Psoriatic Arthritis
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of ustekinumab was assessed in 927 subjects in two randomized, double-blind, placebocontrolled trials in adults with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA). The overall safety profile of ustekinumab in subjects with PsA was consistent with the safety profile seen in clinical trials in adult subjects with plaque psoriasis. A higher incidence of arthralgia, nausea, and dental infections was observed in ustekinumab-treated subjects when compared with placebo-treated subjects (3% vs. 1% for arthralgia and 3% vs. 1% for nausea; 1% vs. 0.6% for dental infections) in the placebocontrolled portions of the PsA clinical trials.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Crohn's Disease
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The safety of ustekinumab was assessed in 1407 subjects with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (Crohn's Disease Activity Index [CDAI] greater than or equal to 220 and less than or equal to 450) in three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter trials. These 1407 subjects included 40 subjects who received a prior investigational intravenous ustekinumab formulation but were not included in the efficacy analyses. In trials CD-1 and CD-2 there were 470 subjects who received ustekinumab 6 mg/kg as a weight-based single intravenous induction dose and 466 who received placebo [see Dosage and Administration (2.3)]. Subjects who were responders in either trial CD-1 or CD-2 were randomized to receive a subcutaneous maintenance regimen of either 90 mg ustekinumab every 8 weeks, or placebo for 44 weeks in trial CD-3. Subjects in these 3 trials may have received other concomitant therapies including aminosalicylates, immunomodulatory agents [azathioprine (AZA), 6-mercaptopurine (6-MP), methotrexate (MTX)], oral corticosteroids (prednisone or budesonide), and/or antibiotics for their Crohn's disease [see Clinical Studies (14.4)].
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5710950
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The overall safety profile of ustekinumab was consistent with the safety profile seen in the clinical trials in adult subjects with plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. Common adverse reactions in trials CD-1 and CD-2 and in trial CD-3 are listed in Tables 6 and 7, respectively.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Other less common adverse reactions reported in subjects in trials CD-1 and CD-2 included asthenia (1% vs 0.4%), acne (1% vs 0.4%), and pruritus (2% vs 0.4%).
blocks.speaker: label
